svg.title: The world, as a kit
svg.desc: Twelve tapering strips of punctuation, joined at the equator, to be cut out and bent into a small paper world. With a moon and a ship, also to be cut out.
svg.text: Twelve pieces, some assembly. It does not turn until you turn it, which makes a change.
Print it. The printer will not mind; it has already been asked for the map, and took that well.
Cut round the outside of the whole strip of twelve. Do not cut the dotted line. That is the equator and the only thing
Bend it into a ring, the far east to the far west. They have never met, and will want a moment.
Bring the points together at the top, each grey tab going under its neighbour. Then the bottom. The Asterisk Caps turn
out to be twenty-four stars each, which is more than anyone had counted.
Cut out the At and hang it on a thread, a hand away. It should be walked round the world once a month. Somebody will have
Fold the Caret along its dotted line and stand it on any part that is not a #. It will fall over. This is the nearest
thing to sailing that paper can do.
The claim is yours. One is supplied, the kit being unable to count to nine. Stick it in where you like; out here nobody
Light is not included. Put it near a window, up and to the left, and it will have a day side like the other one. There is no way back in from here; a kit has no doors.
